title: 2008 AMC 12B 23
statement: The sum of the base-\(10\) logarithms of the divisors of \(10^n\) is \(792.\) What is \(n?\)

solutions.text:
The sum of the base-\(10\) logs of the divisors is the log of their product. A number \(N\) with \(d(N)\) divisors has divisor product \(N^{\frac{d(N)}{2}}.\)

Here \(N = 10^n\) has \(d(N) = (n + 1)^2\) divisors, so the product is \((10^n)^{\frac{(n+1)^2}{2}}\) and its log is \[ \frac{n(n + 1)^2}{2} = 792. \]

Thus \(n(n + 1)^2 = 1584\) \(= 11 \cdot 144\) \(= 11 \cdot 12^2,\) giving \(n = 11.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: The sum of the logs of the divisors equals the log of the product of all divisors
\(10^n\) has \((n + 1)^2\) divisors, and the product of the divisors of \(N\) is \(N^{\frac{d(N)}{2}};\) this gives \(\tfrac12 n(n + 1)^2 = 792\)
